correctness.rationale: For distinct valuations, a unique lowest-valuation summand plus Hensel cube lifting determines local value cosets and their three-vs-seven difference spectrum. For a repeated pair, normalization gives two unit coefficients and a third at valuation 1 or 2. If their ratio is split, a simple local zero gives all local quotients. If nonsplit at p=1 mod3, the smooth genus-one curve alpha X^3+beta Y^3=tZ^3 has an F_p point by Hasse, and cannot have one at infinity, so Hensel proves the binary form represents every p-adic unit. The third term supplies the missing valuation class; quotients span all three residue classes with arbitrary unit parts. For p=2, cubes cover units. For all-three-equal, the standard smooth ternary-cubic zero theorem gives surjectivity. Integer approximation completes the density claim. The finite checker independently checked 47,232 nonsplit mod-p pairs and all 27 difference patterns.

originality.rationale: The new mixed-valuation assertion at p=1 mod 3 with exactly two congruent valuations and a nonsplit binary subform follows from a genus-one Hasse unit-surjectivity lemma, not from the 2021 binary density criterion (which gives the opposite answer for that subform) or the 2022 three-matching-valuation criterion. The full ternary prime-by-prime classification assembles this missing case with previously established cases. Previously known three-equal, split binary, and distinct-residue coset results are explicitly not claimed separately new; residual bibliographic risk is disclosed.

value.rationale: A full prime-by-prime local density criterion for ternary diagonal cubics is a natural missing classification between known binary and three-unit results. The nontrivial new mixed case exhibits a transition from a nonsplit binary non-dense ratio set to a dense ternary ratio set solely by adding a differently valued cubic term. The structural genus-one unit-surjectivity lemma explains the mechanism for all applicable primes rather than offering an arbitrary finite example.
